items: Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027, covering about 26.5 mn workers → higher wages lift consumer spending but raise costs for labour-heavy industries.
TMG Holding's nine-month profit rises 11.9% to EGP 11.72 bn, Fawry's 32% and Edita's 54% → earnings season keeps delivering growth for EGX blue chips.
ONE's container ship crosses the Suez Canal and three more Premier Alliance services are set to follow → the return of Asian carriers adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.
EGX30 rises 0.31% to 52,187 on Sunday, led by Orascom Construction (+3.4%) and AMOC (+4.8%) → the index is up 24.8% this year, though turnover runs 17% below its 90-day average.

Egypt's final IMF review moves to virtual talks with about $2.3 bn at stake before the programme ends on 15 December → the Cairo mission ended without a staff-level deal; a miss would delay funds and could unsettle the pound.
Telecom Egypt's nine-month profit jumps 43.7% to EGP 24.38 bn and Elsewedy Electric's rises 20.7% to EGP 15.30 bn → two large listed companies report strong growth ahead of Sunday's session.

An ENGIE-led group with Orascom Construction closes $588 mn of debt for a 900 MW wind farm at Ras Shokeir → the project doubles the group's wind capacity in Egypt and gives Orascom a construction contract.
Iran says it targets a US base in Bahrain again as Saudi forces down Houthi drones; Brent ends the week at $96.13 → Gulf attacks keep oil high and Egypt's energy bill under pressure.

Trump says the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and tells Vance to drop the talks, while the blockade stays → the end of diplomacy keeps Gulf energy at risk; oil ends the week at $96.13 and European gas jumps 12%.
European gas surges 12% in a week to €96.18/MWh, and Goldman sees €150 in early 2027 if Gulf LNG stays disrupted → costlier LNG raises Egypt's energy import bill and costs for gas-heavy industry.
Gold has its worst week since March, down 4.7%, and 21K gold in Egypt falls 2.7% to EGP 5,950 a gram → markets see a December Fed hike as certain, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 ends the week at 52,023, up about 1.7% (derived), led by banks → QNB Egypt rises four sessions in a row and Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% on Thursday.

Brent jumps 3.3% to $95.82 on Thursday after Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites and Iran's attack on a US radar in Bahrain → renewed attacks on Gulf energy put oil back near $96, a cost for Egypt's import bill.
Gold falls to a 13-month low and is down 3.5% this week; 21K gold in Egypt drops to about EGP 5,975 a gram → markets fully price a December Fed hike, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 falls 0.91% to 52,023 on Thursday, while Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% → blue chips take profits after a strong week; banks with earnings news still rise.
Suez Canal Bank's nine-month profit rises 12.9% to EGP 5.7 bn as interest income grows about 43% → high rates keep lifting bank income.

Israel's security cabinet orders the army to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, and Tehran threatens bases from West Asia to Europe → a renewed war would hit oil, Gulf shipping and the pound just as markets price a wind-down.
Eastern Company's nine-month profit rises 39% to about EGP 9 bn, and the stock gains 4.17% → sales rise 11% and margins widen, which supports the stock.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,500 on Wednesday after two days of gains, with turnover at EGP 11.79 bn → the rally pauses as small caps take profits; fertiliser stocks rebound.
The government targets public debt of about 69.5% of GDP by 2030 and frees a Red Sea plot to help pay it down → lower debt would ease debt-service costs over time.

key.l: gas price increase for seven fertiliser makers

stories.h: Fertiliser makers pay 50% more for gas in exchange for full export rights
stories.what: Seven fertiliser producers agree to a temporary rise in their gas price to $12.75 per mmBtu from $8.50 for 45 days from 16 November, paying $175 mn upfront. In return they can export all current output until early January and are exempt from supplying subsidised fertiliser to the Agriculture Ministry. Gas cuts of 20-40% stay, and Abu Qir is shutting one of its three plants. The state pays about $28 per mmBtu for LNG and has cut November cargoes from 15 to six.
stories.why: Imported gas costs far more than the urea it makes, so the state passes on part of the cost.
stories.aff: Fertiliser margins, urea exports and the state's LNG bill.
stories.eg: The deal keeps export dollars flowing but raises costs for the sector.
stories.egx: Bearish for fertiliser margins; export volumes are protected for now.

stories.h: Small caps slide as the EGX30 holds flat at 52,200
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Arab Finance; StockAnalysis.com
stories.what: The EGX30 edges up 0.02% to 52,199.83 on Monday while the EGX70 falls 3.76% and the EGX100 2.88%. Turnover is EGP 11.15 bn and market cap falls to EGP 4.15 tn. Egyptians and foreigners net buy while Arabs net sell EGP 161.7 mn. Edita (+7.44%), Telecom Egypt (+5.19%) and Eastern (+2.90%) gain, while MOPCO (-4.10%), Palm Hills (-3.42%) and EFG Holding (-3.21%) fall.
stories.why: The sources give no single cause for the small-cap drop.
stories.aff: Small caps, retail investors and blue chips.
stories.eg: Gains concentrate in a few large names.
stories.egx: Bearish for small caps; neutral for the blue-chip index.
stories.names: Edita, Telecom Egypt, Eastern (up); MOPCO, Palm Hills, EFG Holding (down).

stories.h: Edita posts record quarterly revenue and a 41.5% profit rise
stories.what: Edita's third-quarter revenue rises 32.9% to EGP 7.3 bn and net profit 41.5% to EGP 938.1 mn. Packs sold rise 18.5% to 1.2 bn and export sales 23.6% to EGP 673.6 mn. Nine-month profit rises 54% to EGP 2.4 bn. The stock rises 7.44% to EGP 20.66 on Monday.
stories.why: Higher volumes, pricing and mix, led by cakes and bakery, and a growing Iraq business.
stories.aff: Edita's valuation and the snack market.
stories.eg: Strong local demand for packaged food despite inflation.

key.l: Gemini services returning to the Suez Canal

stories.h: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move three more services back to the Suez Canal
stories.what: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd will route three Gemini services, AE1, AE2 and AE3, through the Suez Canal instead of around the Cape of Good Hope. The first sailings leave Ningbo on 4 December, Shanghai on 20 December and Shanghai on 14 January. Maersk said in October it expects all its services back on the canal by March 2027.
stories.why: The shorter route improves transit times between Asia, Europe and the Middle East.
stories.aff: Canal revenue, port services and Egypt's dollar income.
stories.eg: More transits add dollar revenue and support the pound.
stories.egx: Bullish for shipping, port and logistics names.

stories.h: Oil slips to $92 as supply catches up with demand
stories.what: Brent falls 44 cents to $92.00 and WTI to $85.28 on Tuesday morning as recovering Middle East exports outweigh attacks on tankers. The IEA sees a return to surplus in the fourth quarter, OPEC+ meets on 29 November to set 2027 output, and US strategic reserves fall to their lowest since 1982. "Supply has finally caught up with demand," says KCM Trade's Tim Waterer.
stories.why: Gulf exports recover even as Hormuz attacks continue.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill and the pound.
stories.eg: Brent near $92 eases Egypt's fuel costs.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for importers and energy users.
